subject: Critical Thinking
title: Charles Darwin: Thinking Through Deep Time
description: Learn Charles Darwin: Thinking Through Deep Time in one minute.

hook.text: Darwin had no modern lab, just notebooks, specimens, and patience.

buildup.text: His method: patient observation over decades, meticulous data collection, & the courage to follow evidence to its.

discovery.text: Darwin waited 20 years to publish 'Origin of Species' – testing, gathering more evidence, anticipating objections.

twist.text: He feared the social consequences. Evolution contradicted the biblical creation story.

climax.text: Darwin's lesson: follow evidence even when it's uncomfortable.

punchline.text: He delayed publication for years because the idea was explosive.

quiz.question: Why did Darwin wait 20 years to publish his theory of evolution?
options: To gather overwhelming evidence and anticipate objections, making the case unassailable
He didn't think it was important

details.summary: Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection was built on decades of meticulous observation, classification, and reasoning. He deliberately sought out evidence that contradicted his theory, modeling intellectual honesty at its finest.
details.whyItMatters: Darwin's process — not just his conclusion — is a masterclass in critical thinking: patient observation, willingness to follow evidence, and active search for disconfirming data.
takeaways: Darwin spent decades gathering evidence before publishing
He actively sought evidence that would disprove his theory
His method combined observation, classification, and deduction

faq.question: Why did Darwin wait over 20 years to publish his theory of evolution?
faq.answer: He knew the idea was revolutionary and controversial, so he wanted overwhelming evidence. He also feared the social consequences. His hand was forced when Alfred Russel Wallace independently arrived at a similar theory.

faq.question: How did Darwin practice disconfirmation as part of his scientific method?
faq.answer: Darwin kept a special notebook of observations and arguments against his theory. He believed that contradictory evidence was easy to forget, so he wrote it down immediately. This habit forced continuous refinement of his ideas.
